title: Persistent Spontaneous Time-Reversal Breaking
abstract: We provide an analytic realization of spontaneous parity and time-reversal breaking without thermal restoration in a local, unitary, ultraviolet-complete quantum field theory in $2+1$ dimensions with finitely many fields. The theory is defined by a relevant Yukawa deformation of a product of the critical biconical vector model and free massless Dirac fermions. This deformation induces a renormalization group flow whose infrared endpoint is a decoupled product of the critical vector model and the conformal Gross-Neveu-Yukawa model. At zero temperature, the vacuum preserves both symmetries, whereas upon heating, the theory undergoes an inverse thermal transition at a finite critical temperature. Above this temperature, a fermion mass, odd under parity and time reversal, is dynamically generated, and the broken phase persists to arbitrarily high temperatures.
summary: This work analytically demonstrates a quantum field theory exhibiting spontaneous parity and time-reversal symmetry breaking that persists even at arbitrarily high temperatures. Using the large-N expansion in 2+1 dimensions, the authors analyze the thermal phase transition, showing that the symmetry breaking emerges upon heating rather than being present at zero temperature. This provides a controlled theoretical framework for studying non-trivial thermal phase transitions.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide an analytic realization of spontaneous parity and time-reversal breaking (PSSB) in a quantum field theory without the symmetry breaking being restored by finite temperature.
main_result: The theory exhibits a persistent spontaneous breaking of parity and time-reversal symmetry above a critical temperature, surviving to arbitrarily high temperatures.
method: The analysis uses the large-N expansion, finite-temperature effective potential calculations, and renormalization group flow techniques to study the phase structure.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum field theory in 2+1 dimensions, defined by a Yukawa deformation coupling a critical biconical vector model to free massless Dirac fermions.
key_observables: The thermal expectation value of the field $\langle\chiangle_T$, and the persistence of a fermion mass odd under parity and time reversal.
important_parameters: The critical temperature ($T_{crit}$), the large-$N$ limit, and the coupling constants governing the Yukawa interaction.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-N expansion and assumes the system is away from narrow parametric windows where finite-N corrections dominate.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the model, analyzing the RG flow from a UV CFT to an IR fixed point, and then performing a detailed finite-temperature analysis using the large-N saddle-point approximation to determine the phase transition.
why_interesting: The study of symmetry breaking persistence at high temperatures is a core topic in statistical mechanics, particularly relevant for understanding high-energy phase transitions in condensed matter systems.
